correctness.rationale: Petersen is triangle-free of diameter two and all edges extend to two-edge geodesics. An overlapping pair of auxiliary edges has exactly one common Petersen neighbor, the complementary pair of unused labels; the 30 maximal geodesics thus correspond to spanning P₃ plus a disjoint K₂ in K₅. If the unselected auxiliary graph has no isolates and contains a matching of size two, the fifth label has a neighbor on the matching and creates that forbidden triple. Otherwise its edges are pairwise intersecting, and only the full star (not a triangle) can avoid isolates on all five labels. This gives precisely star-containing transversals and the five separate six-edge complements themselves. The listed sets are minimal because no star lies in a six-edge complement and removing any edge of one such complement makes it infeasible. Inclusion-exclusion over star centers and addition of the five uncovered complements produce coefficients (5,30,80,90,45,10,1) in degrees four through ten, summing to 261. For b≤6 the branches over different stars are disjoint and have no inclusion edges between them; each truncated star branch is connected and has 1, 7, or 22 states, and a six-edge minimal complement is isolated when b=6. At b=7 two stars meet via their union of size seven, while a six-edge complement missing the v-star attaches by adding uv to complete the u-star. There are 205 states up to budget seven. The lower bound of six toggles between distinct stars is met by the union route.
